findings.summary: Every bend of a branch is drawn as its own annotate call, so each of a branch's three segments carries its own arrowhead and shrinks back from its neighbour: a reader sees one head end in mid-air below the gate (pointing at the branch line rather than at a box) and another head at each elbow pointing along the horizontal into the corner, with a 4-5 px break before the short vertical stub that enters the box. Both branches are affected: on the no branch the horizontal head's tip is at x=1033 and the vertical stub runs at x 1038-1041, and on the yes branch the horizontal head's tip is at x=525 against the stub at x 518-521. The routing still reads - gate, yes/no, then the box each arm lands in - so this does not hold the node; one arrowhead per branch, placed at the path end rather than per segment, would remove it.

rubric_items.data_ink: Passes. The ink carries the drawing and nothing else: two reader boxes feeding the 'any *.json in runs/ ?' gate, the yes and no branches beneath it, the two destination boxes, one explanatory sentence, a four-line note block and three dot-and-text rows for the measured arms. There is no chart chrome, no grid, no legend frame and no redundant mark; the 3 pt blue outline on the run-store box is the one highlighted path, which is the subject the figure exists to show.
rubric_items.decoration: Passes. The canvas, all four boxes and the note block are plain white; the note block carries a thin #cccccc outline and nothing else. There is no gradient, background fill, shading, drop shadow or styled theme anywhere in the render, and the only filled marks are the three 8 px arm dots, which encode the reverted read, the base arm and the head arm.
rubric_items.label_collision: Passes. No label is clipped and none overlaps another label or the data. rubric_items.legibility: Passes. Readable at a glance: 'ledger readers' over its two reader lines, an arrow into the gate question, the yes and no branches, the two titled boxes 'per-run documents + aggregate' and 'run store' with the rule each follows beneath its title, one sentence stating that both sources answer one population, and the three measured arms as a left-aligned dot-and-text list whose revisions and pass counts are legible without magnification.
rubric_items.table_form: Passes. The image is a source-precedence drawing rather than a table dressed as boxes: it shows which source answers a reader and no column of values. The three arms are three one-line statements with a coloured dot, and the reader-coverage table the caption points at lives in the evidence fragment, so the figure does not reproduce tabular data.
